name: W3C AI Agent Protocol Community Group
status: Active Community Group (created 2025-05-08); agent identity is DID-method-agnostic (did:wba, did:web, did:webvh) since 2026-08-13. Bi-weekly meetings; the meeting of 2026-10-07 was announced as canceled (calendar notice of 2026-10-01), and a meeting was held on 2026-10-21, whose minutes were added to the repository on 2026-10-22; the W3C group data list two chairs. Pull request #46, "Add Agent Authorization specification", opened on 2026-10-21, was open and not merged on 2026-10-23, with no comments or reviews; two ways of identifying the agent as an OAuth client were discussed (a DID as the client identifier, or the HTTPS client identifier of a Client ID Metadata Document bound to a DID), and no choice between them is recorded; commits of 2026-10-22 to the pull request move it to DID-associated Client ID Metadata Document URLs. On 2026-11-02 PR #46 is still open and not merged. The group's white paper ("Agent Network Protocol White Paper", CG-DRAFT, index.html last changed on 2026-01-14) compares MCP, A2A, ANP, Agent Connect Protocol and Agent Communication Protocol; UCP, AP2, x402 and commerce are not found in it (read 2026-11-02). The agenda of the meeting of the W3C Autonomous Agents on the Web Community Group (WebAgents) at TPAC on 2026-10-26 (Dublin, 09:00 to 12:30) includes a talk by this group's co-chairs; no minutes were found in the WebAgents repository on 2026-11-02. WebAgents, created 2023-03-20, studies Web-based multi-agent systems built on Linked Data and hypermedia, and its charter says "No specifications will be produced under the current charter."
relevance: The protocol draft defines an Agent Discovery Service Protocol in JSON-LD, with active discovery at https://{domain}/.well-known/agent-descriptions and an Agent Description "Information" that covers "products, or services". The use_case.html draft includes a hotel booking scenario (Personal Agent, Search Agent, hotel Service Agent) with the requirement "Agent Transactions". The agent identity draft uses a Decentralized Identifier (DID) URL as the HTTP signature keyid with RFC 9421 and RFC 9530.

committed_next.what: Topics "streaming HTTP authentication, mutual DID authentication"; joint Technical Plenary and Advisory Committee (TPAC) session with the WebAgents Community Group (CG) under discussion

boundary: On 2026-09-10 the maintainer wrote of a proposal on agent memory "My feeling is that this goes beyond the current scope of our protocol.".
participation: The author of this map posted the map on the group's public list on 2026-10-15 and replied there the same day to a proposed addition; the chair reviewed that message at the group meeting of 2026-10-21 (minutes), which the author did not attend; see Disclosure.
